sanskrit: dvādaśāraṃ nahi taj jarāya varvarti cakraṃ pari dyām ṛtasya | ā putrā agne mithunāso atra sapta śatāni viṃśatiś ca tasthuḥ ||
english: The twelve-spoked wheel of Ṛta rolls around heaven, never subject to decay. O Agni, upon it stand paired sons — seven hundred and twenty.

sanskrit: pañcapādaṃ pitaraṃ dvādaśākṛtiṃ diva āhuḥ pare ardhe purīṣiṇam | atheme anya upari vicakṣaṇaṃ saptacakre ṣaḍara āhur arpitam ||
english: They call the five-footed, twelve-formed Father full-bodied in the upper half of heaven; others above declare him, the far-seeing, fixed on the seven-wheeled, six-spoked [wheel].

sanskrit: pañcāre cakre parivartamāne tasminn ā tasthur bhuvanāni viśvā | tasya nākṣas tapyate bhūribhāraḥ sanād eva na chidyate sanābhiḥ ||
english: As the five-spoked wheel turns round and round, all worlds are established upon it. Its axle glows with the immense burden; from of old the nave is never severed.

sanskrit: sanemi cakram ajaraṃ vi vāvṛta uttānāyāṃ daśa yuktā vahanti | sūryasya cakṣū rajasaity āvṛtaṃ yasminn ā viśvā bhuvanāny ārpitā ||
english: The ageless wheel with unbroken felly revolves; ten yoked [steeds] draw it upon the outstretched [sky]. Covered, the eye of the Sun moves through the atmosphere — upon it all worlds are fastened.

sanskrit: sākaṃjānāṃ saptatham āhur ekajaṃ ṣaḍ id yamā ṛṣayo devajā iti | teṣām iṣṭāni vihitāni dhāmaśaḥ sthātre rejante vikṛtāni rūpaśaḥ ||
english: The seventh of those born together they call the only-born; six, they say, are the twin-born ṛṣis, offspring of the gods. Their oblations are distributed station by station; differing in form, they shine in the steadfast [realm].

sanskrit: striyaḥ satīs tām̐ u me puṃsa āhuḥ paśyad akṣaṇvān na vi cetad andhaḥ | kavir yaḥ putraḥ sa īm ā ciketa yas tā vijānāt sa pituṣ pitāsat ||
english: Those who are women — men call them such; the seeing one with eyes perceives it, the blind does not discern. The son who is a seer recognises them; he who knows them would be the father of his own father.

sanskrit: avaḥ pareṇa para enāvareṇa padā vatsaṃ bibhratī gaur ud asthāt | sā kadrīcī kaṃ svid ardhaṃ parāgāt sā kva svit sūte nahi yūthe asmin ||
english: Below the farther, above the nearer, bearing the calf on her hoof, the cow has arisen. Facing downward, to which side has she gone? Where does she calve? — for she is not in this herd.

sanskrit: avaḥ pareṇa pitaraṃ yo asya- -anuveda para enāvareṇa | kavīyamānaḥ ka iha pra vocad devaṃ manaḥ kuto adhi prajātam ||
english: Who knows his father below the farther, above the nearer — who, acting as seer, could here declare whence is born the divine mind?

sanskrit: ye arvāñcas tām̐ u parāca āhur ye parāñcas tām̐ u arvāca āhuḥ | indraś ca yā cakrathuḥ soma tāni dhurā ni yuktā rajaso vahanti ||
english: Those moving hither — them they call moving yonder; those moving yonder — them they call moving hither. O Soma, those things which you and Indra made: yoked to the pole they carry [the load] through the atmosphere.

sanskrit: dvā suparṇā sayujā sakhāyā samānaṃ vṛkṣaṃ pari ṣasvajāte | tayor anyaḥ pippalaṃ svādv atty anaśnann anyo abhi cākaśīti ||
english: Two fair-winged companions, yoked together as friends, cling around the same tree. One of the two eats the sweet pipal berry; the other, eating nothing, only looks on.

sanskrit: yasmin vṛkṣe madhvadaḥ suparṇā niviśante suvate cādhi viśve | tasyed āhuḥ pippalaṃ svādv agre tan non naśad yaḥ pitaraṃ na veda ||
english: In the tree where the honey-eating fair-winged birds nest and all bring forth their young — they say its sweet pipal berry is at the crest; he who does not know the Father will not attain it.

sanskrit: yatrā suparṇā amṛtasya bhakṣam animeṣaṃ vidathābhisvaranti | ino viśvasya bhuvanasya gopāḥ sa mā dhīraḥ pākam atrā viveśa ||
english: Where the fair-winged ones chant unblinking at the assembly for a share of immortality — the Lord, the guardian of all the world — that wise one has entered into the simple one right here.

sanskrit: yad gāyatre adhi gāyatram āhitaṃ traiṣṭubhād vā traiṣṭubhaṃ niratakṣata | yad vā jagaj jagaty āhitaṃ padaṃ ya it tad vidus te amṛtatvam ānaśuḥ ||
english: That which in the gāyatrī was placed beyond the gāyatrī, and the triṣṭubh that was fashioned out from the triṣṭubh — and the verse that was set in the jagatī's jagatī — those who truly know that have attained immortality.

sanskrit: gāyatreṇa prati mimīte arkam arkeṇa sāma traiṣṭubhena vākam | vākena vākaṃ dvipadā catuṣpadā- -akṣareṇa mimate sapta vāṇīḥ ||
english: With the gāyatrī one measures the ark; with the ark the sāman; with the triṣṭubh the speech. With speech they measure speech — two-footed, four-footed — with the syllable they measure the seven voices.

sanskrit: jagatā sindhuṃ divy askabhāyad rathantare sūryaṃ pary apaśyat | gāyatrasya samidhas tisra āhus tato mahnā pra ririce mahitvā ||
english: With the jagatī [metre] he propped the celestial river; in the rathantara [sāman] he beheld the Sun round about. They speak of three kindling-sticks of the gāyatra; by that greatness it surpassed all in majesty.

sanskrit: upa hvaye sudughāṃ dhenum etāṃ suhasto godhug uta dohad enām | śreṣṭhaṃ savaṃ savitā sāviṣan no 'bhīddho gharmas tad u ṣu pra vocam ||
english: I call near this good-milking cow; may the skilled-handed milker milk and draw from her. May Savitṛ press out for us the choicest pressing; the gharma kindled — of that I now proclaim aloud.

sanskrit: hiṃkṛṇvatī vasupatnī vasūnāṃ vatsam icchantī manasābhy āgāt | duhām aśvibhyāṃ payo aghnyeyaṃ sā vardhatāṃ mahate saubhagāya ||
english: Making the hiṃkāra sound, mistress of the Vasus, seeking her calf she came near in thought. May this inviolable one be milked of her milk for the two Aśvins; may she increase to great good fortune.

sanskrit: gaur amīmed abhi vatsaṃ miṣantaṃ mūrdhānaṃ hiṅṅ akṛṇon mātavā u | sṛkvāṇaṃ gharmam abhi vāvaśānā mimāti māyuṃ payate payobhiḥ ||
english: The cow lowed toward her calf blinking its eyes; she made the hiṃ-sound at the calf's head, eager to be its mother. Lowing toward the brimming gharma vessel, she bellows her cry, overflowing with milk.

sanskrit: ayaṃ sa śiṅkte yena gaur abhīvṛtā mimāti māyuṃ dhvasanāv adhi śritā | sā cittibhir ni cakāra martyaṃ vidyud bhavantī prati vavrim auhata ||
english: This is he who bellows, by whom the cow, covered all around, lows her cry, perched on the quivering [hide]. She, by her wisdom, laid low a mortal; becoming lightning, she hurled herself against the covering.

sanskrit: vidyud dadrāṇāṃ salilasya pṛṣṭhe yuvānaṃ santaṃ palito jagāra | devasya paśya kāvyaṃ mahitvādyā mamāra sa hyaḥ sam āna ||
english: Lightning, slumbering on the back of the waters, though young, was devoured by the grey one. Behold the poetic power of the god in his greatness — today he died, yet yesterday he came together.

sanskrit: anac chaye turagātu jīvam ejad dhruvaṃ madhya ā pastyānām | jīvo mṛtasya carati svadhābhir amartyo martyenā sayoniḥ ||
english: The breathing one lies still; the swift-footed, the living, the trembling, the steadfast — in the midst of dwellings. The living moves by his own powers among the dead; the immortal shares a womb with the mortal.

sanskrit: apaśyaṃ gopām anipadyamānam ā ca parā ca pathibhiś carantam | sa sadhrīcīḥ sa viṣūcīr vasāna ā varīvarti bhuvaneṣv antaḥ ||
english: I saw the herdsman who does not rest, going hither and thither along the paths. Putting on convergent and divergent [forms] alike, he revolves again and again within the worlds.

sanskrit: ya īṃ cakāra na so asya veda ya īṃ dadarśa hirug in na tasmāt | sa mātur yonā parivīto antar bahuprajā nirṛtim ā viveśa ||
english: He who made it does not know it; he who saw it — the sight has been hidden from him. Wrapped within the womb of the mother, he of many offspring has entered into dissolution.

sanskrit: dyaur naḥ pitā janitā nābhir atra bandhur no mātā pṛthivī mahīyam | uttānayoś camvor yonir antar atrā pitā duhitur garbham ādhāt ||
english: Heaven is our father, our begetter, our navel here; kin to us is this great Earth, our mother. The womb lies between the two outstretched bowls; here the father placed the embryo in the daughter.

sanskrit: pṛcchāmi tvā param antaṃ pṛthivyāḥ pṛcchāmi tvā bhuvanasya nābhim | pṛcchāmi tvā vṛṣṇo aśvasya reto vācaḥ pṛcchāmi paramaṃ vyoma ||
english: I ask you: what is the farthest limit of the earth? I ask you: what is the navel of the world? I ask you: what is the seed of the vigorous horse? I ask you: what is the highest heaven of speech?

sanskrit: iyaṃ vediḥ paro antaḥ pṛthivyā ayaṃ yajño bhuvanasya nābhiḥ | ayaṃ somo vṛṣṇo aśvasya reto brahmāyāṃ vācaḥ paramaṃ vyoma ||
english: This altar-ground is the farthest limit of the earth; this sacrifice is the navel of the world. This Soma is the seed of the vigorous horse; this brahman is the highest heaven of speech.

sanskrit: saptārdhagarbhā bhuvanasya reto viṣṇos tiṣṭhanti pradiśo vidharmaṇi | te dhītibhir manasā te vipaścitaḥ paribhuvaḥ pari bhavanti viśvataḥ ||
english: The seven half-embryos, the seed of the world, stand in Viṣṇu's law in the [four] quarters. Those wise ones, those far-seeing ones, encompass with their thoughts and minds; they surround on every side.

sanskrit: na vi jānāmi yad ivedam asmi niṇyaḥ sannaddho manasā carāmi | yadā māgan prathamajā ṛtasya- -ād id vāco aśnuve bhāgam asyāḥ ||
english: I do not discern what it is that I am; hidden, girded up, I wander with the mind. When the first-born of Ṛta came to me, then at last I obtained a share of this speech.

sanskrit: apāṅ prāṅ eti svadhayā gṛbhīto 'martyo martyenā sayoniḥ | tā śaśvantā viṣūcīnā viyantā ny anyaṃ cikyur na ci cikyur anyam ||
english: Going away, yet forward, seized by his own inherent power, the immortal shares a womb with the mortal. They two, ever going apart in opposite directions, perceive the one but not the other.

sanskrit: ṛco akṣare parame vyoman yasmin devā adhi viśve niṣeduḥ | yas tan na veda kim ṛcā kariṣyati ya it tad vidus ta ime sam āsate ||
english: In the imperishable supreme heaven where all the gods have settled — he who does not know that, what will he do with the ṛc? Those who truly know that, they are seated here together.

sanskrit: ṛcaḥ padaṃ mātrayā kalpayanto 'rdharcena cākl̥pur viśvam ejat ||
english: Fashioning the footing of the ṛc by measure, with the half-verse they have fashioned all that moves. The triple-footed brahman manifests in many forms; by it the four quarters live.

sanskrit: sūyavasād bhagavatī hi bhūyā atho vayaṃ bhagavantaḥ syāma | addhi tṛṇam aghnye viśvadānīṃ piba śuddham udakam ācarantī ||
english: May you become full of blessing from good pasture, and may we in turn be blessed. Eat the grass, O inviolable one, at all times; drink of the pure water, going about freely.

sanskrit: gaurīr mimāya salilāni takṣaty ekapadī dvipadī sā catuṣpadī | aṣṭāpadī navapadī babhūvuṣī sahasrākṣarā bhuvanasya paṅktis tasyāḥ samudrā adhi vi kṣaranti ||
english: The gaurī has measured out and fashions the waters — she who is one-footed, two-footed, four-footed. Having become eight-footed, nine-footed, of a thousand syllables is the meter of the world; from her the oceans flow forth.

sanskrit: athāpād eti prathamā padvatīnāṃ kas tad vāṃ mitrāvaruṇā ciketa | garbho bhāraṃ bharaty ā cid asya ṛtaṃ piparty anṛtaṃ ni pāti ||
english: Then the footless goes first among those with feet — who of you two, O Mitra and Varuṇa, has perceived that? The embryo bears the burden even of him; it fulfils Ṛta and wards off what is not Ṛta.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇaṃ niyānaṃ harayaḥ suparṇā apo vasānā divam ut patanti | tā āvavṛtrant sadanād ṛtasya- -ād id ghṛtena pṛthivīṃ vy ūduḥ ||
english: Along the dark path the tawny fair-winged ones, clothed in waters, fly up to heaven. They turned back from the seat of Ṛta; and therewith they bedewed the earth with ghee.
